recipes.name: Peachy Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 1 (29 ounce) can sliced peaches, drained and syrup reserved

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Trim all visible fat from chops and season with salt and pepper to taste. Brown chops in vegetable oil.

Combine reserved peach syrup, brown sugar, and ginger. Pour over chops and bring to a boil. Add peaches and cook, uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes or until liquid is reduced to half and thick. Turn chops occasionally to ensure even cooking. Serve!

raw_recipe.headline: Peachy Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Peaches are infused with a dash of ginger and a touch of brown sugar to make a delectable sauce for pan-fried pork chops in this fast and easy dinner.

review.reviewBody: You can bake this recipe if you want to prepare it and walk away for an hour or so. Bake covered at 300 degrees F. Also, I enhanced the seasonings by rubbing each chop with a blend of cardomom, ground ginger, salt and pepper prior to browning. My kids and husband RAVED about the finished product.

I loved it, taking the suggestions of others regarding adding more spice and a little cornstarch for thickening. Even my teenager liked it! I added a bit of garlic salt, cinnamon and ginger to the spice rub prior to frying, and then chopped up two dried chili peppers and a little more garlic to the sauce as it simmered. Easy-peasy and SO good! Thanks, Waybet!

PERFECT! Super easy to make and very tasty! As written it is very good. Only things I changed were based on my personal preference...sprinkled some cayenne powder on chops for a little kick while they browned, added 2 tsp soy sauce to peach syrup and lastly, added a corn starch slurry (1/4 c water to 2 tbsp corn starch) in the last 5 min to make sauce thicker.

Great base recipe! Like other reviewers suggested, I added a few things: 2 tbsp soy sauce, 3 cloves minced garlic, , and 1 tsp cinnamon. Also, after the 15 minutes of cooking down, I removed the pork and added a water/corn starch mixture -- mixed before adding to pan (1/4c water to 2 tbsp corn starch). Absolutely yum!!!

I used 4 chops, used a 15 oz can of peaches, took others advice and added garlic and soy sauce and some orange juice. Browned in skillet then baked in oven 300 degrees for 1 hour. Will be making again for sure! We served it over medium egg noodles and there was plenty of sauce. Great dinner!!!

We had this version for dinner last night,except I made it with a pork roast in my slow cooker.
I also added balsamic vinegar to balance the sweetness just a bit(2tbsp) we really liked the flavour
of the sauce but the roast turned out a little dry ( 6hrs on high ) will only cook for 5 hrs next time. I still would give five stars for easy, tasty and hands off.

I made this twice today with a little variation. Following the recipe exactly was too sweet and a bit greasy even for my children. So I omitted the brown sugar and added 2-3 Tbs of soy sauce, 10 peperoncino, and half a glass of wine and it turned out wonderful.

Normally, if we have fruit with chops, we have apples. This was a nice change. I followed the recipe exactly, except I used sliced peaches in juice, not sugar, and my chops were not as thick as recommended by the author. If you are in the same boat with your chops, just cook them to an internal temperature of 145º, and take them out of the skillet. You can let the sauce continue to cook and thicken as the chops rest under foil. DH thought the dish was tasty, and I liked the slightest zing of ginger with the peaches.

This is very good. I had a leftover pork loin chip already grilled. I sliced it up and added it to the peaches and sauce along with some chopped red bell pepper and crushed pepper flakes. Served over rice. Excellent.

I used this recipt to use up some fresh peaches I had that were getting soft. Like other reviewers suggested, I used OJ for the liquid and also added soy sauce. The chops were ready before the sauce thickened so I took them out, turned up the heat on the sauce, and thickened it with a bit of cornstarch. This had a very nice flavor!

Can I give this one six stars? It was super easy, fast, and a nice way to change up the usual pork chop dinner. Based on other suggestions, I added about 1 1/2 tsp garlic and about 2 tbs of soy sauce, and bit more ginger. YUM!!!! I did find that the sauce didn't thicken very much, perhaps because I used 2 15 oz. cans of peaches and reserved a good amount of the peaches for snacking... I added a touch of cornstarch to the sauce and the result was perfection! I'd definitely recommend this to the busy weekday cook who needs a new way to jazz up pork chops.

Took the advice of the reviews and bumped up the spices. I added McCormick sunshine all-purpose seasoning by Tabitha Brown. It had garlic, ginger, pineapple, and mango, which was perfect for the peaches. This is a keeper.

This was a very quick and easy dish to prepare that my husband and I both enjoyed and agreed it worth repeating . I used boneless pork chops and I added garlic powder along with the salt and pepper. I used canned peaches in juice that I roughly chopped before adding to the pan. We served with rice and mixed steamed vegetables, for a complete meal.
Wonderful, I added 1/4 tsp red pepper flake, and that was just what it needed.
Served with rice and green beans.
This was a simple, but flavorful meal. I added a knob of fresh ginger instead of dried since I had it. I’ll make this again!
Surprisingly easy and tasted great. I also added thesoy sauce and a splash of wine.
Fast easy and very good
This is easy and amazing. My family doesn't like to stray too far from "traditional" recipes, and it was a hit for everyone!
I made 2 servings with smoked pork chops and it came out wonderfully. I served it with wild rice and a salad. Umm, um, yummy.
